diagnostic_evidence.quote: For any $\epsilon>0$, the operator $\mathcal{T}_{\epsilon,\#}$ is positive, because $|S(x)| \geq c_\epsilon >0$ for all $x \in \overline{D} \backslash \overline{Y}_\epsilon$.

Combining \eqref{RIeps}, \eqref{RIf} and \eqref{RIl}, we obtain the range identity
$
\mbox{Range}\,(F_{\#}^{1/2})=\mbox{Range}\,(L).
$

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 2.2 asserts that Range(F_#^{1/2}) = Range(L) under the relaxed assumption that |S| > 0 a.e. on D (allowing inf_{x in D} |S(x)| = 0). The proof attempts to justify this by taking limits of domains D \ \overline{Y}_\epsilon and asserting that norm convergence of operators implies convergence of their ranges in (2.8) and (2.10), which is mathematically invalid. Moreover, the claim itself is false: when inf_{x in D} |S(x)| = 0, the middle multiplication operator T_# fails to be coercive on L^2(D) (violating hypothesis (ii) of Theorem A.1), and Range(F_#^{1/2}) = Range(L T_#^{1/2}) is strictly smaller than Range(L) whenever 1/sqrt{|S|} is not in L^2(D).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict Assumption 1.1 to the standard uniform lower bound |S(x)| >= c > 0 on \overline{D}, restoring the coercivity of T_# and enabling the application of the established range identity from GGH2022.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 2.2 is unestablished and false as stated when the source function approaches zero inside or on the boundary of D.
issues.title: Invalid proof and failure of range identity under non-coercive middle operator
issues.why_classification: The repair requires withdrawing one of the paper's explicitly advertised contributions (item (iii) in Section 1.3: weakening the positivity condition to |S| > 0 a.e.) and excluding the advertised regime where the source vanishes on a set of measure zero.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Choose the set $\{y_m\}_{m=1}^{\infty}$ such that $y=y_1$.Then we have $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L_N)$ for all $N\geq 1$. By Lemma \ref{lem4.1} (ii), it holds that $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L)$.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 3.1 claims that z in K_{D,eta}^{(x_hat)} if and only if \phi_{z,eta}^{(x_hat)} in Range(L). In reality, \phi_{z,eta}^{(x_hat)}(k) = e^{-i k b} is never in Range(L) for any z in R^3 or eta in R. For any u in L^2(D), (Lu)(tau) is the Fourier transform of a compactly supported 1D L^2 function (the slice integrals of u), which must belong to L^2(R) by Plancherel's theorem; however, tau -> e^{-i tau b} has constant absolute value 1 on R and is not square-integrable. The authors' proof relies on Lemma 3.2(ii) (lem4.1), which invalidly claims that Range(L) = lim_{N -> \infty} Range(L_N) and infers membership in Range(L) from membership in finite-dimensional approximations Range(L_N). Consequently, by Picard's theorem the series in the indicator function I_eta^{(x_hat)}(y) diverges for all y in R^3, rendering W_eta identically zero.

failure_location.quote: For any $\eta \in \R$, there holds $z \in {K}_{D,\eta}^{(\hat{x})}$ if and only if $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must abandon pointwise plane-wave test functions and replace them with mollified or spatially integrated test functions (such as indicator functions of small balls in D), which requires a completely different analytical framework for the indicator functions.
issues.overall_effect: The characterization of the strip via Range(L) fails, causing the indicator functions in Section 4, the identification of pulse moments and strips (Theorems 4.1-4.3, 4.5), and the resulting uniqueness results (Theorems 4.4, 4.6, Corollary 4.7) to fail.
issues.title: Pointwise plane-wave test functions never belong to the range of the data-to-pattern operator
issues.why_classification: The failure invalidates the entire inversion framework and all subsequent reconstruction and uniqueness guarantees; resolving it requires abandoning the advertised pointwise test functions and developing new proof architecture.
